record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Explore the applications of the probabilistic method in the scope of pattern avoidance.

evidence.quote: Explore the applications of the probabilistic method in the scope of pattern avoidance. The so-called circular words were also concerned by some conjectures:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the set of finite words over A. A pattern is a word p over a separate alphabet of variables E = {e_1, e_2, ...}. A word w in A* is said to encounter the pattern p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : E* -> A* such that h(p) appears as a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p. The pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some alphabet of size k that avoids p, and the avoidability index lambda(p) is the smallest such k (infinity if no such k exists).

The probabilistic method, in particular variants of the Lovász Local Local Lemma (including the entropy compression / Moser–Tardos framework), provides a general technique for proving the existence of infinite words avoiding prescribed sets of forbidden factors when each long enough factor has only "few" forbidden extensions.

Develop and exploit applications of the probabilistic method (Lovász Local Lemma, entropy compression, and related tools) to problems of pattern avoidance in words. In particular, for as broad a class of patterns p as possible, obtain new upper bounds on the avoidability index lambda(p), and on the related quantities for avoidance of patterns in the abelian, k-abelian, or additive sense, and for avoidance of patterns by circular (necklace) words. Determine to what extent such probabilistic arguments can match or improve the bounds known from explicit morphic constructions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research direction rather than a single sharply posed conjecture. Probabilistic techniques (Lovász Local Lemma, entropy compression introduced by Moser–Tardos and applied to non-repetitive sequences by Grytczuk, Kozik, Micek, and to pattern avoidance by Ochem, Pinlou, and others) have produced many partial results since 2013, but as a general program the exploration is ongoing and considered open.

status_evidence.title: New approach to nonrepetitive sequences (Grytczuk, Kozik, Micek)
status_evidence.snippet: Entropy compression method applied to nonrepetitive sequences, giving a probabilistic proof and improved bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Probabilistic/entropy-compression techniques have been actively applied to pattern avoidance in words, but the general program remains open-ended.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of patterns (Ochem et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Uses probabilistic and entropy-compression arguments to bound avoidability indices of patterns.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists; the broad exploration suggested is ongoing.
